extracted.intended_audience: Army and DoD contracting and oversight officials, installation contracting officers, TRADOC, and congressional oversight staff
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating whether an OMB Circular A-76 conversion (in-house vs contract) realized projected savings and whether the resulting contract is being administered and monitored properly (including award-fee administration, productivity measurement, cost updates, and readiness impacts).

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 cost study requirement (compare in-house vs contractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 requires commercial activities be studied to determine whether they could be done more economically by private contractors or by government employees; a cost study compares estimated contract and in-house costs to determine the more cost-effective approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use OMB's Cost Comparison Handbook for computing cost comparison amounts; follow DoD Instruction 4100.33 and Army Regulation 5-20 for implementation; include contract administration, one-time conversion, and additional costs when computing total contract costs; deduct federal income taxes and Social Security and savings plan costs as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management study / Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsible activity must do a management study to determine how the in-house work force should be organized and equipped to most efficiently do the work; the MEO models how the in-house work force should operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MEO staffing and performance become the baseline (standard) for measuring productivity and for defining minimum government requirements used in the A-76 comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a Performance Work Statement (PWS)
rubrics_metrics.description: The activity is to develop a performance work statement — a description of the required work — as part of the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PWS defines the government's required work and is the basis for contractor performance expectations and award-fee evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) required
rubrics_metrics.description: A government quality assurance surveillance plan is required for measuring actual contractor performance if contracting out is chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign QA evaluators (QAEs) to monitor operations; use the plan to issue discrepancy reports and to provide the objective basis for award-fee determinations and potential cure/termination actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare government estimate of lowest required employees and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The activity is to prepare a document containing the government's estimate of the lowest number and types of employees required to do the work described in the PWS, and from these data prepare a total estimated cost for in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These in-house estimates form the government side of the A-76 cost comparison and must be defensible and consistent with MEO assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total cost comparison composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Total contract costs should include the contract price and contract administration, one-time conversion, and additional costs; certain items (federal income taxes, Social Security, savings plan costs) are deducted to arrive at total contract costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all relevant cost elements are included and transparently documented; updating cost bases to current fiscal-year data is necessary to avoid underestimating contract costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion differential (10 percent margin) rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract is to be awarded if the total projected cost to contract out is less than the government's estimate and the margin of difference by the contractor is more than 10 percent of the estimated in-house personnel costs (conversion differential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the threshold is met, the government workforce is reassigned or terminated; use consistent methodology to compute the percentage and document Appeals Board adjustments if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions remain in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherently governmental functions — those intimately related to the public interest — are to continue to be done by federal employees and not contracted out under A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and exclude inherently governmental functions during the analysis and PWS drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award-fee plans must motivate performance exceeding minimum (FAR/DFARS)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAR and DFARS contemplate that an award-fee structured contract is to provide a contractor motivation for performing at a level exceeding the minimum acceptable performance level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure award-fee criteria so higher scores correspond to performance above minimum standards; include incentives for cost control and excellence; avoid formulations that make 'meeting minimum' equivalent to top score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not pay award fees for minimum or below-minimum performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-fee provisions should not be administered so that contractors receive the entire award fee for meeting — not exceeding — minimum contract standards, nor receive portions of award fees for performance below minimum standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administration that pays for meeting or below-minimum performance removes the incentive for excellence and can lead to paying substantial fees for inadequate performance (Ft. Sill example: paid award fees for less-than-minimum performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Align award-fee scoring so 100 means exceeding standards, not merely meeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Award-fee scoring must be calibrated so that the top score represents performance above the minimum acceptable standard rather than merely meeting it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scoring schemes where a score of 100 equates to meeting baseline in-house performance; provide explicit scoring-to-fee mappings that reward exceeding standards and penalize below-minimum results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision monitoring and recompete requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB's supplement to the circular requires that A-76 contracts be monitored to ensure they continue to be cost effective; if contract costs become unreasonable, the agency is to recompete the contract, and if recompetition fails to result in reasonable prices and in-house performance is feasible, a new A-76 study should be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish monitoring triggers and procedures to detect when costs have become unreasonable; DoD Instruction 4100.33 was criticized for lacking criteria on when to resolicit — agencies should define objective thresholds and timelines for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and triggers for discrepancy reports and corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: QAEs are to issue discrepancy reports when (1) one major safety or security violation occurs, (2) three instances of noncompliance with established standards occur without corrective action, or (3) five or six minor operations problems occur without corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use discrepancy reports as the documented basis for contractor corrective-action plans, cure notices, or termination decisions; repeated discrepancies should escalate enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursable payment rules for cost-plus-award-fee contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: In a cost-plus-award-fee contract, the government is to reimburse the contractor for allocable, allowable, and reasonable costs to operate the function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contract administration verifies that costs billed are allocable/allowable/reasonable; include cost-control incentives in award-fee structure to discourage unnecessary reimbursable spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service Contract Act (SCA) prevailing wage treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Service Contract Act requires federal contractors to pay their employees not less than the prevailing minimum wage as determined by the Department of Labor; bids and in-house estimates do not include future wage increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate that prevailing wage increases will require contract modifications to reimburse contractors for higher wages, and account for this potential in post-award monitoring and projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update cost bases to current fiscal-year data before finalizing contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs used in the A-76 study based on older fiscal-year data must be updated to reflect the costs at the time the contractor actually begins work; failure to update can result in substantial cost increases (example: update from FY85 to FY88 added $7.7 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures for timely cost updates and reflect changes in negotiated price or contract modifications prior to or shortly after award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cost-control incentives in award-fee plans
rubrics_metrics.description: A properly structured award-fee plan should include incentives for controlling costs as well as for quality/performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design award-fee plans to balance incentives for improved performance and for cost containment; modifications (e.g., December 1989) can add such incentives if initially absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure contractor productivity against MEO-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity should be measured against standards established from the in-house MEO; reductions in productivity directly affect labor costs and equipment readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track productivity metrics over time; quantify cost impacts of reduced productivity (example: Northrop averaged ~82% of standard leading to ~$1.8M excess costs and projected additional $4.5M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment readiness benchmarks for deployability
rubrics_metrics.description: For a unit to be considered fully deployable/ready for combat, at least 90 percent of its equipment must be available; readiness ratings below that indicate impaired deployability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use readiness metrics to assess operational impact of contractor performance; compare pre- and post-conversion readiness (example: pre-conversion >90% vs contractor-supported average ~85%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-level oversight and follow-up of directed changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Army headquarters and TRADOC should follow up on their directions to installations (for example, to revise award-fee provisions) to ensure the instructions were implemented and to monitor for performance problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish oversight mechanisms to detect whether local contracting officers implement required changes and to identify systemic problems early; lack of follow-up contributed to award-fee misadministration at Ft. Sill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require contractor improvement plan when performance is deficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The contracting officer should require the contractor to provide, within a specific time frame, a plan that demonstrates how it proposes to meet minimum performance standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the plan and determine next steps (e.g., monitoring, additional contractual remedies, or termination) if the plan is inadequate or not implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish objective criteria for resolicitation/recompetition when costs exceed in-house estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD Instruction 4100.33 was found not to provide criteria for determining when contract costs exceed in-house estimates enough to warrant resolicitation; agencies should define those thresholds and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify implementing instructions to include policies/procedures requiring services to resolicit contracts or initiate a new A-76 study when costs exceed in-house estimates by defined amounts or under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect and handle confidential in-house cost figures appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: In-house cost figures used for decisionmaking and potential future A-76 studies may be treated as confidential by the activity contemplating a new study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While maintaining confidentiality where necessary, ensure sufficient transparency for oversight and for comparisons; confidential status can limit external audit detail but should not prevent accountability.
